population.span: consecutive adult patients admitted for elective cardiac surgeries randomly received a 1-mg dose of colchicine (n = 81) or placebo (n = 71) orally 12 to 24 hours before surgery followed by a daily dose of 0.5 mg until hospital discharge.

endpoint.span: The primary efficacy endpoint was the development of at least one episode of AF (lasting 5 minutes or longer) occurring after cardiac surgery at any point during hospitalization.

estimate.span: The rate of AF was 16.0% (n = 13) in the colchicine group, versus 18.3% (n = 13) in the placebo group. Comparing the colchicine and placebo groups, the odds ratio was 0.85 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.37–1.99).

ci.span: Comparing the colchicine and placebo groups, the odds ratio was 0.85 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.37–1.99).

analysis_set.span: Among the 152 randomized patients, AF occurred in 26 patients (17%), including 16% of patients in the colchicine group and 18.3% of patients in the placebo group.

treatment_strategy.span: Upon enrollment, patients were treated with 1 mg of colchicine or matching placebo 12 to 24 hours prior to surgery, followed by colchicine (0.5 mg) or placebo immediately after their surgery (via a nasogastric tube) and daily treatment at this dose until hospital discharge.
